jobs.title: Project Manager - Natural Gas Projects
jobs.description:
We’re a team of friends bound together by a mission to preserve our planet for future generations through innovative energy solutions and modern infrastructure. Intersect develops, constructs, and operates the most ambitious power and data center infrastructure in the country by co-locating industrial demand with dedicated gas and renewable power generation.

Intersect was acquired by Google in March 2026 and operates as an independent subsidiary. We are developing and constructing multiple gigawatts of energy and data center projects in the U.S., enabling more data center and generation capacity to come online faster. We’re on an aggressive growth trajectory and looking for people hungry to tackle the largest energy challenges on the planet.

Location & Team Gatherings

Intersect has been a fully flexible workplace since its founding in 2016.  We’ve been very intentional about the way we do things. We are not work-from-home, hybrid, or in-office - we are any and all of those options! Deepening social connections and offering shared experiences is a cornerstone of the way we work. We connect as a team at our Team Week experiences four times a year and at our recently established Hub locations - SF Bay Area, NYC Metro Area, NY; Denver, CO; Austin, TX; Calgary, AB; and Toronto, ON.

We are currently looking for candidates located within 60 miles of any of the listed hubs to foster more in-person connections while maintaining our flexible remote culture.

About This Role

As part of Intersect’s project delivery organization, you’ll lead the execution of critical power generation and energy infrastructure projects that support the convergence of electrification, digitalization, and decarbonization. Acting as the owner’s representative throughout the project lifecycle, you’ll guide complex projects from development through commissioning and commercial operation while partnering closely with engineering, construction, commercial, operations, and executive leadership teams.

You’ll oversee the successful delivery of natural gas-fired power generation facilities and related infrastructure, including reciprocating engine plants, gas turbine facilities, HV switchyards, substations, battery energy storage systems (BESS), generation assets, and large-scale data center power infrastructure. Success requires strong technical judgment, disciplined project execution, and the ability to align diverse stakeholders around safety, quality, schedule, budget, and long-term value creation.

This role is planned to start as soon as practical based on project requirements. A training and onboarding period of approximately two weeks is anticipated, with the expectation that the successful candidate will contribute immediately, become actively engaged during the first week, and achieve full organizational integration within the first two months.

Team Overview

This team plays a critical role in advancing Intersect’s mission to accelerate the clean energy transition through the development and execution of large-scale energy infrastructure projects. By bringing together expertise across development, engineering, construction, commercial operations, and asset management, the team delivers the integrated infrastructure required to support a more reliable, scalable, and sustainable energy future.

Joining this team provides the opportunity to work on highly visible projects with significant industry impact while collaborating alongside experienced professionals who are shaping the next generation of energy infrastructure. The team values accountability, innovation, continuous learning, and cross-functional partnership, creating an environment where individuals can grow professionally while contributing to meaningful outcomes.

What You’ll Do

Lead Complex Project Execution

Develop and execute comprehensive project plans, including scope definition, execution strategy, resource planning, governance structures, and delivery objectives.

Lead natural gas-fired power generation projects from development through commissioning and commercial operation.

Drive project performance against key objectives related to safety, quality, schedule, budget, and operational readiness.

Facilitate project closeout activities, lessons learned, commissioning support, and successful turnover to operations teams.

Manage EPC and External Partner Performance

Serve as the primary owner’s representative and point of contact for EPC contractors, consultants, utilities, equipment vendors, and key stakeholders.

Oversee contractor performance, contract compliance, commercial negotiations, change management activities, and claims resolution.

Review and approve construction strategies, procurement plans, and execution methodologies.

Build productive relationships across complex stakeholder groups to support successful project outcomes.

Drive Project Controls and Risk Management

Develop and maintain project schedules, budgets, forecasts, risk registers, and reporting frameworks.

Implement project controls processes that improve visibility into cost, schedule, and execution performance.

Lead risk identification, mitigation planning, and issue resolution activities throughout the project lifecycle.

Provide clear, actionable project updates to senior leadership and executive stakeholders.

Deliver Technical Excellence

Partner with engineering teams to review and approve technical designs, engineering deliverables, vendor submittals, and construction approaches.

Support the integration of reciprocating engine facilities, gas turbine plants, HV substations and switchyards, utility interconnections, BESS assets, generation resources, and data center infrastructure.

Ensure technical solutions align with project objectives, operational requirements, and long-term asset performance expectations.

Drive quality assurance and quality control processes across engineering, procurement, construction, and commissioning activities.

Champion Safety and Regulatory Compliance

Foster a culture of safety excellence across all project activities and stakeholder groups.

Conduct site inspections, audits, and field reviews to verify adherence to safety requirements, project specifications, and quality standards.

Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, environmental obligations, permitting requirements, and applicable energy-sector standards.

Support safe and compliant project execution while maintaining a focus on continuous improvement and operational excellence.

Build Alignment Across Teams

Partner with engineering, construction, commercial, operations, and executive leadership teams to drive decision-making and project success.

Facilitate collaboration across internal and external stakeholders to resolve challenges and maintain project momentum.

Promote accountability, transparency, and strong communication throughout project execution.

Help cultivate a high-performing environment centered on technical excellence, ownership, and long-term value creation.

What You’ll Bring

Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Architectural Engineering, Construction Management, or a related engineering or design discipline.

10+ years of progressive experience in project execution, construction management, engineering management, or project leadership within power generation, energy infrastructure, oil & gas, utility, or heavy industrial sectors.

Demonstrated experience executing projects from either the Owner’s side or Contractor/EPC side through development, engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operational handover.

Direct experience supporting the construction and execution of natural gas-fired power generation projects.

Knowledge of quality assurance, commissioning, startup activities, and safety management systems.

Exceptional communication, stakeholder management, negotiation, and leadership skills.

A hands-on leadership style that balances strategic oversight with detailed execution and accountability.

Resilience, sound judgment, and composure when navigating competing priorities and complex stakeholder environments.

A commitment to collaboration, continuous learning, inclusion, and long-term value creation aligned with Intersect’s values of Equity, Humility, Authenticity, Long-run Value, and People Come First.

Total Rewards

Total Compensation:
$188,500 - $205,400 (total compensation includes base salary + bonus in USD)

Equity:
Beyond your salary, you’ll receive an Equity Grant, giving you a meaningful stake in our parent company. 

Health & wellness:
100% premium coverage for you and your dependents on medical, dental, and vision

Time to recharge:
Unlimited PTO, plus two company-wide breaks (Fourth of July & end of year)

Family support:
Up to 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, plus 6 additional weeks for birth parents; access to family planning and family care support through Carrot and Maven

Mental health:
Free access to Spring Health, including 5 free therapy and psychiatry sessions, plus a Headspace account for mindfulness and meditation through our physical health vendor, Wellhub+

Perks & extras:
$150 monthly food stipend, $150 monthly reimbursement for cell phone and internet, pet insurance allowance, full home office setup, free access to UrbanSitter with $625 in quarterly company-paid credits, ActiveHero, and One Medical

All employees share in the responsibility for fulfilling Intersect's commitment to equal employment opportunity. Intersect does not discriminate against any employee or applicant on the basis of age, ancestry, citizenship, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, immigration status, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran or military status, race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by and consistent with applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances. We adhere to these principles in all aspects of employment, including recruitment, hiring, training, compensation, promotion, benefits, social and recreational programs, and discipline.

This
hybrid

jobs.title: Staff Technical Program Manager - Vision AI
jobs.description:
Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission.

By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale.

With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order.

Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures.

Most TPM roles focus on tracking timelines, coordinating milestones, and driving execution against an established plan. This role is different. You’ll own the operational backbone of a vision AI data program, ensuring ideas move seamlessly from hypothesis to data capture to validation to a governed dataset to a commercial product.

You’ll sit at the center of a complex ecosystem spanning a lean founding engineering team, capture hardware and annotation vendors, frontier AI and robotics companies, academic partners, and internal Legal, Site Operations, and Finance teams. Your mandate is to create operational continuity across these interfaces, remove friction, accelerate decisions, and maintain a disciplined path from experimentation to validated, production ready outcomes.

Stord Labs is an innovation center designed to evaluate emerging logistics technologies and help redefine the future of fulfillment. Within a live micro fulfillment environment, you’ll orchestrate the full lifecycle of technical experiments, ensuring promising concepts are rigorously tested, clearly validated, and efficiently transitioned into production when they demonstrate measurable business value.

This role is built for a systems oriented program leader who has operated in computer vision, ML, AI, robotics, or data intensive environments and can translate fluently between research, engineering, and warehouse operations without sacrificing speed or precision. You’ll be equally comfortable working with engineers and researchers, coordinating external partners, navigating operational constraints, and communicating outcomes to executive stakeholders.

The goal isn’t simply to manage the program. It’s to build the operating system that allows a new vision AI capability to move from idea to validated data product at scale.

What You'll Do

Own the evaluation lifecycle: Govern the end to end pipeline of experiments, ensuring every initiative starts with a clear hypothesis, measurable success criteria, and structured evaluation framework. Drive disciplined decisions to kill, iterate, or scale based on evidence.
Run hardware and vendor evaluations: Lead structured, evidence based evaluations across capture devices, depth sensors, gloves, edge compute, and data and annotation vendors. Own RFPs, scorecards, evaluation frameworks, and vendor selection.
Orchestrate the cross functional ecosystem: Serve as the primary integration point between the engineering pod and Legal, Site Operations, Finance, and warehouse operations. Coordinate requirements around consent, associate participation, scheduling, floor logistics, cost modeling, and operational readiness.
Manage the data pipeline program: Drive the path from pilot capture through annotation, validation, and secure buyer delivery. Own annotation throughput and QA cadence while establishing and tracking data quality, capture yield, and delivery metrics.
Manage partners and buyers: Coordinate technical and operational engagement with frontier AI and robotics companies and academic partners such as Georgia Tech. Translate customer requirements into clear program priorities and ensure datasets meet the standards required for validation and delivery.
Keep governance and risk on track: Ensure consent, privacy, and data rights requirements are addressed with Legal before and throughout capture activities. Identify and retire program risks while keeping executive sponsors informed of progress, tradeoffs, and decisions.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Industrial Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related technical discipline.
8+ years of experience in Technical Program Management, Engineering Management, or complex cross functional delivery roles.
Demonstrated experience running computer vision, ML, or data pipeline programs end to end, including data collection, annotation, model training pipelines, or data platform delivery.
Proven experience managing both hardware and data or annotation vendors, including RFPs, structured evaluations, scorecards, and strategic partnerships.
Comfortable operating in deeply technical CV, ML, and data environments and translating between research, engineering, and operations without losing precision.
Strong execution discipline and experience operating in agile, sprint based, or similar environments.
Demonstrated judgment in making and driving kill, iterate, or scale decisions based on data and outcomes.
High ownership and comfort operating in ambiguous, 0 to 1 environments.

Bonus Points

Experience in innovation labs, R&D environments, or advanced automation programs.
Familiarity with egocentric or robotics datasets, annotation platforms such as Scale, MLOps, or delivering datasets to external customers.
Experience with data governance, privacy, or consent programs, including BIPA, GDPR, or CCPA requirements.
Familiarity with warehouse data ecosystems and architectures, including WMS, OMS, WES, and WCS.
Exposure to digital twin or simulation initiatives.
Domain knowledge in warehouse automation, robotics integration, or fulfillment operations.
Experience working with frontier AI companies, robotics companies, academic research institutions, or other emerging technology partners.

This role can be located at any major Northrop Grumman site and Remote work/hybrid work will be considered for the ideal candidate.

We are seeking an Enterprise COTS Implementation Specialist to lead the evaluation, pilot, and deployment of commercial off‑the‑shelf (COTS) tools across Contracts Management. This role is responsible for planning and running pilots/proof‑of‑concepts, integrating new tools with existing internal business systems, and driving full-scale implementation in partnership with CIDO and business stakeholders. The ideal candidate has hands‑on experience with enterprise tool rollouts, understands complex business processes, and can effectively work across functions, sectors, and organizations to ensure adoption and value realization.

Lead end‑to‑end COTS tool implementations, from requirements and vendor evaluation through deployment and transition to operations.
Plan, execute, and evaluate pilots/proof‑of‑concepts to validate technical fit, usability, and business value.
Collaborate with architects and system owners to integrate new tools with existing internal business systems and data sources.
Partner with cross‑functional stakeholders across multiple sectors and organizations to gather requirements, manage expectations, and drive adoption.
Develop implementation plans, training materials, and change management approaches to support successful rollout.
Identify risks, issues, and dependencies and coordinate mitigation with technical and business teams.

Associate's degree with 14 years of experience, or Bachelor's degree with 12 years of experience, or Master’s degree with 10 years of experience; a High School diploma or equivalent and 16 years of experience may be considered in lieu of a completed degree.
Demonstrated experience implementing COTS tools in an enterprise environment.
Proven track record running pilots/proof‑of‑concepts, including success criteria definition and outcome analysis.
Understanding of internal business systems and integrations (e.g., ERP, PLM, HR, or other core enterprise platforms).
Ability to work effectively across functions, sectors, and organizations, building consensus among diverse stakeholders.
Demonstrated project coordination skills, including planning, communication, and status reporting.

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge of our internal business systems including contracts management, legal, finance and ERP tools
Ability to tie AI into systems requirements as we look at new potential solutions

As a Data Center Implementation Manager, you will lead the end-to-end execution of multiple concurrent data center infrastructure projects, spanning Greenfield builds, colocation white space fit-outs, equipment upgrades, and lifecycle replacements. You’ll serve as the single point of contact for all construction activities on your assigned projects, coordinating closely with data center providers, MEP contractors, and internal stakeholders.

Your role includes overseeing construction schedules and budgets, managing OFCI equipment procurement and installation, conducting design reviews, and driving alignment across cross-functional teams including electrical, mechanical, low voltage, and network engineering. Project Leadership & Oversight:
Manage the build out of multiple data center projects concurrently, from detailed design to physical build out, including Greenfield construction projects, colocation white space fitouts, equipment upgrades, and end-of-life replacements. Proven experience managing data center construction projects, including Greenfield builds, colocation fit-outs, and infrastructure upgrades.

Passionate about continuous improvement and staying current with industry trends, technologies, and best practices in data center design and delivery.

Proven track record managing full lifecycle data center projects, colocation fit-outs, and infrastructure upgrades.

Deep understanding of mechanical, electrical, and low voltage systems, with experience reviewing OFCI submittals and coordinating with design and construction teams.

This role will focus on managing global compliance projects, optimizing processes, and ensuring the successful integration of trade compliance requirements into Husky’s systems.

You will partner with cross-functional teams—including Supply Chain, Engineering, IT, Finance, and Sales—to strengthen Husky’s global trade compliance framework, enhance operational efficiency, and reduce compliance risk across all regions.

Program and Project Management

Lead the planning, execution, and delivery of global trade compliance initiatives, including process optimization, technology integration, and system enhancements.

Manage the implementation of trade compliance modules within the ERP system to ensure alignment with global regulatory requirements.

Establish and maintain project governance, milestones, KPIs, and reporting mechanisms for trade compliance programs.

Coordinate global stakeholders to ensure timely completion of key deliverables and consistent global deployment of compliance practices.

Regulatory Compliance and Oversight

Translate complex regulatory requirements into actionable business processes and internal controls.

Collaborate with Engineering and Legal teams to establish export control measures and export authorization processes globally.

Monitor the effectiveness of trade compliance procedures and implement corrective actions as needed.

Classification, Licensing, and Documentation

Lead efforts to standardize global product classification processes, including export control, HTS, and country-of-origin determinations.

Develop and maintain processes for end-use/end-user certifications, license applications, and transaction due diligence.

Ensure accuracy and consistency in trade data, documentation, and system configurations supporting export and customs compliance.

Risk Management and Continuous Improvement

Conduct global risk assessments and audits to evaluate compliance performance and identify improvement opportunities.

Develop risk mitigation strategies to prevent export control or import customs violations.

Drive continuous improvement initiatives leveraging digital tools and automation to enhance compliance monitoring and reporting.

Support internal investigations and voluntary disclosures, when applicable.

Training, Communication, and Stakeholder Engagement

Develop and deliver global training programs to increase awareness of export control, sanctions, and customs requirements.

Promote a culture of compliance through proactive communication and cross-functional collaboration.

Partner with IT, Supply Chain, and Finance to ensure trade compliance considerations are embedded in business processes.

Provide input in communications with government authorities and external consultants regarding trade compliance projects and inquiries.

Required Experience & Education

10+ years of progressive experience in global trade compliance, covering export controls, customs, sanctions, and trade agreements.

Deep understanding of U.S., EU, and Canadian export control and sanctions laws, with additional experience in UK, Swiss, Chinese, and other jurisdictions considered an asset.

Proven track record in managing large-scale trade compliance or ERP integration projects within a multinational organization.

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, International Business, Law, Supply Chain, or related discipline; PMP or other project management certification preferred.

Strong analytical and organizational skills, with the ability to interpret complex regulations and translate them into practical business solutions.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, capable of influencing and engaging stakeholders across multiple levels and functions.

Demonstrated ability to lead change, manage competing priorities, and deliver results under tight deadlines in a global environment.

jobs.description:
About Us

Johnson Controls, a global leader in thermal management, mission-critical building systems, energy efficiency, and decarbonization, helps customers use energy more productively, reduce carbon emissions, and operate with the precision and resilience required in rapidly expanding industries such as data centers, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, advanced manufacturing, and higher education.

For more than 140 years, Johnson Controls has delivered performance where it really matters. Backed by advanced technology, lifecycle services and an industry-leading field organization, we elevate customer performance, turn goals into real-world results and help move society forward.

HVAC Controls Project Manager

Johnson Controls is a global leader in smart, healthy, and sustainable buildings, and this role supports the delivery of HVAC control systems that help customers improve performance, reliability, and comfort. As an HVAC Controls Project Manager, you will lead projects from planning through closeout while balancing technical execution, customer communication, safety, and financial results.

Role Overview

Under general direction, you will act as the on-site project leader for assigned HVAC controls projects. You will coordinate the full lifecycle of the work, from design and programming through commissioning, documentation, billing, and warranty handoff, while maintaining strong customer relationships and supporting profitable project delivery.

Key Responsibilities

Lead assigned control systems projects from planning and execution through final closeout.
Coordinate hardware design, system programming, installation activities, system and network commissioning, and project closeout.
Direct subcontractors, electrical installers, technicians, designers, and administrative support as needed to complete the work.
Maintain responsibility for project financial performance, including costs, billings, collections, profitability, and cash flow.
Communicate with customers throughout all phases of the project and pursue change orders when scope or conditions change.
Ensure work performed complies with applicable state, local, and federal requirements and is completed with the highest ethical standards.
Oversee the selection, ordering, budgeting, and delivery of project materials and coordinate vendor and subcontractor pricing.
Provide site-specific training, accurate documentation, as-built information, manuals, and warranty support upon completion.

How You Will Do It

Own the outcome by staying accountable for scope, schedule, cost, safety, and integrity from kickoff through completion.
Evaluate contractual scope, field directives, bulletins, and schedule changes carefully, then translate them into clear project actions and change order opportunities.
Complete or delegate hardware design and software programming using established standards, then validate system functionality until the installation operates as intended.
Provide accurate commissioning records, as-built documentation, and jobsite coordination so field installation matches project requirements.
Stay close to the work by working directly with customers, subcontractors, and internal teams to remove obstacles and resolve issues quickly.
Track progress with regular updates, monthly forecasts, and clear communication to management regarding revenue, cost, and gross margin expectations.
Improve every day through candid problem-solving, learning from field conditions, and tightening coordination across design, execution, and administration.
Win as one team by building trust across all partners, sharing technical guidance, and valuing different perspectives that improve project delivery.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Expansion
jobs.description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

Waymo’s Technical Program Managers and Program Managers are accountable for Waymo’s roadmap execution by providing thoughtful cross-functional planning, clarity, and proactive risk management. In the face of complex technical and operational challenges with no established playbooks to follow, we act with thoughtful urgency, driving conversations, discussions, and outcomes. Our team partners closely with every function of Waymo to structure, own and drive work towards real-world deployments of the Waymo Driver across platforms and geographies.

This role follows a hybrid work schedule and reports to the Program Manager Lead, Commercialization and Expansion.

You Will

Lead and launch expansion programs for new markets and new horizontal / vertical capabilities
Drive and own plans and critical path for market launch activities
Orchestrate deliverables, scope and timelines across internal teams including Product, Engineering, GTM, Legal, and Operations
Establish new or improve existing workflows and processes to build a strong foundation for the org to grow and scale
Proactively identify and reduce both short- and long-term business-critical risks and dependencies
Keep stakeholders informed and aligned; represent programs from senior leadership to execution teams;escalate effectively when needed to remove blockers

You Have

5+ years of experience managing highly complex cross-functional programs
Experience driving large programs with a holistic understanding of business-wide functions (ie. Product, Eng, Legal, External Engagement, etc) and the ability to manage deliverables between organizations
Strong leadership skills to manage both upstream and downstream dependencies.
Clear verbal and written communication, alongside the ability to navigate ambiguity and drive decision-making in a fast-paced environment
Significant expertise in identifying breakdowns and scaling processes within complex, growing areas that impact the future of the organization and how the team functions.

We Prefer

Expertise in external partner engagement and market expansion (e.g. scale, commercialization)
Expertise within SW program management
Expertise within autonomous vehicles or automotive space
Experience scaling businesses
Experience launching in national and international markets
Experience with road safety, design, or transportation planning

Actual starting pay will be based on job-related factors, including exact work location, experience, relevant training and education, and skill level. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for the role location or, if the role can be performed remote, the specific salary range for your preferred location, during the hiring process.

Waymo employees are also eligible to participate in Waymo’s discretionary annual bonus program, equity incentive plan, and generous Company benefits program, subject to eligibility requirements.

$159,000—$196,000 USD

Job Title –Product Owner

Job Location: Bangalore, India

About Company:

ThermoFisher Scientific Inc. is the world leader in serving science, with revenues of more than $40 billion and approximately 1,20,000 employees globally. Our Mission is to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer. We help our customers accelerate life sciences research, solve complex analytical challenges, improve patient diagnostics, deliver medicines to market and increase laboratory productivity.

About Team
: We are Automation, AI and Data (AAD) team that caters to data engineering and analytics, automation and AI solutions for various groups and divisions within Thermofisher Scientific.

What will you do?

As a product owner, you will play a key role in strengthening our data engineering capabilities delivering data engineering pipelines and solutions through Enterprise Data Platform (EDP) for various groups and divisions.

General Job Functions

Product Ownership & Roadmap Management
Own and prioritize the Data Engineering product backlog based on business value, risk, dependencies, and technical feasibility.
Define product objectives, roadmap, milestones, acceptance criteria, and measures of success.

Business Requirement Translation
Partner with Supply Chain, Finance, Data Owners, Data Stewards, SMEs, IT teams, and other stakeholders to understand business problems.
Translate business requirements and data-quality rules into clear user stories, technical requirements, data rules, and acceptance criteria for Data Engineers.

Data Analysis & Validation
Perform hands-on SQL analysis to understand datasets, investigate data-quality issues, validate engineering outputs, and support root-cause analysis.
Define and validate data-quality controls covering completeness, consistency, business rules, reconciliation, duplicates, exceptions, and outliers. These are particularly relevant to the supplied UOM audit procedures.

Data Engineering Collaboration
Work closely with Data Engineers to design and deliver reliable data pipelines, curated datasets, data-quality solutions, and analytical data products.
Participate in discussions involving Databricks, PySpark, SQL, data transformations, source-to-target mappings, data models, and pipeline dependencies.

Stakeholder & Cross-Functional Management
Act as the primary bridge between business stakeholders and technical teams.
Facilitate requirement workshops, backlog refinement, sprint planning, demos, issue resolution, and stakeholder updates.
Communicate technical concepts, limitations, risks, and trade-offs in business-friendly language.

Data Quality & Governance
Establish data-quality requirements, validation rules, exception-management processes, and remediation workflows.
Collaborate with Data Owners and Data Stewards to establish accountability and appropriate review/approval processes for master-data changes.

Business Domain & Value Alignment
Understand how data supports Supply Chain processes such as demand planning, inventory planning, procurement, product/master data and ERP operations, as well as related Finance measures.
Ensure engineering priorities are connected to measurable outcomes such as inventory accuracy, planning accuracy, operational efficiency, data-quality improvement, and cost savings.

Testing, Release & Adoption
Define acceptance criteria and coordinate business/UAT validation of engineering deliverables.
Validate that delivered datasets and data products meet functional requirements before release and monitor adoption, data quality, and business outcomes after implementation.

Must Have Skills And Experience

Strong SQL skills – ability to write complex queries involving joins, CTEs, aggregations, window functions, reconciliation, exception identification, and data-quality analysis.
Data Engineering understanding – solid understanding of ETL/ELT, data pipelines, data transformations, data models, data warehouses/lakehouses, source-to-target mappings, and data-quality frameworks.
Databricks & PySpark familiarity – working knowledge of the Databricks environment and ability to understand PySpark notebooks/code and discuss transformation logic with Data Engineers. Deep software-engineering expertise is not required.
Product Owner / Agile experience – demonstrated ability to manage product backlogs, write user stories and acceptance criteria, prioritize requirements, and work effectively with engineering teams in Agile delivery models.
Stakeholder communication & requirement management – strong ability to work across technical teams, business SMEs, leadership, Data Owners and Data Stewards and translate between business and technical terminology.

Good to have skills

Hands on experience with Snowflake or Azure data engineering.
Knowledge of SQL and NoSQL databases like PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB Cassandra.
ERP and Master Data experience
Data visualization experience using tools such as Power BI or Tableau.
Relevant certifications in data engineering on cloud platforms.
Basic understanding of machine learning and Generative AI concepts.

As one team of 1,20,000 colleagues, we share a common set of values - Integrity, Intensity, Innovation and Involvement - working together to accelerate research, solve complex scientific challenges, drive technological innovation and support patients in need.

Lead enterprise-level requirements strategy by partnering with senior business leaders, product owners, and cross-functional teams to define, refine, and prioritize complex business needs across programs and value streams.
Manage product-level backlogs and support roadmap planning by evaluating business value, strategic objectives, dependencies, risks, team capacity, and investment priorities.
Serve as a strategic liaison among business stakeholders, development teams, and leadership while facilitating discovery sessions, requirements workshops, prioritization discussions, and continuous feedback loops.
Collaborate with Agile Scrum teams to analyze business requirements and translate them into actionable user stories, acceptance criteria, and high-quality technology solutions.

Develop comprehensive product documentation and champion Agile and SAFe best practices through business cases, capability models, process flows, decision logs, requirements governance, and continuous improvement activities.

Demonstrated expertise in Electronic Data Interchange transactions, including hands-on experience analyzing, interpreting, mapping, and validating EDI data within complex enterprise workflows.

jobs.description:

CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: Yes

CLEARANCE TYPE: Top Secret

TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman Space Systems—Missile Defense Integration offers an excellent opportunity for a Computer Operations Analyst – Global COSA (26-407)
to join our team of skilled and diverse professionals. Based at Schriever Space Force Base, CO, this role is essential to supporting the U.S. President, the Secretary of Defense, and combatant commanders at the strategic, regional, and operational levels.

This position does not provide relocation assistance and requires on-site work with no remote options.

Position Overview

The Command and Control, Battle Management, and Communications (C2BMC) program is a key component of the Missile Defense System. It is a vital operational system that enables the U.S. president, the Secretary of Defense, and combatant commanders at strategic, regional, and operational levels to plan ballistic missile defense operations systematically, collectively monitor the battle, and dynamically control networked sensors and weapon systems to achieve global and regional mission goals. C2BMC supports layered missile defense capabilities that enable an optimized response to threats across all ranges and flight phases. It serves as a force multiplier by networking, integrating, and synchronizing autonomous sensor and weapon systems and operations, both globally and regionally, to improve performance. C2BMC is essential for all ground and flight tests that verify and demonstrate the current and future capabilities of missile defense systems.

As a Global Computer Operations Support Analyst (COSA‑G), you will be part of a high‑performing team that performs daily system monitoring, operations, and maintenance of the C2BMC‑G systems in a 24x7 operations and test environment. You will provide first‑level technical support, help ensure continuous mission readiness, and play a critical role in real‑world and test events that enable Space Domain Awareness and Space Defense.

Essential Functions

Perform daily monitoring, operations, and maintenance of C2BMC‑G mission and training systems in a 24x7 environment supporting operational and training missions at the Missile Defense Integration & Operations Center (MDIOC)
Provide first‑level technical support to the customer and perform initial troubleshooting of local C2BMC‑G hardware, software, and network issues
Monitor, analyze, and document system and network events; accurately report issues and status to leadership promptly
Receive tasking and direction from leadership for all operations, test, and real‑world events, ensuring procedures and mission timelines are followed
Assist in the maintenance and administration of user accounts as directed by the local ISSO, supporting proper access control and security practices
Coordinate with internal and external agencies to troubleshoot data flow issues and establish or restore network connectivity
Operate and sustain the C2BMC‑G mission systems and/or training systems environment, ensuring availability, performance, and reliability for supported missions
Follow established processes and contribute to continuous improvement of operational runbooks, procedures, and documentation
Perform other duties and assignments as required to support C2BMC‑G operations and the broader Missile Defense mission

Basic Qualifications

Please list your current security clearance and IAT or relevant certifications on your resume, if applicable.

A Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, or a related field from an accredited university, along with 2 years of experience; or a Master’s degree in a related field with 0 years of relevant work experience; or 6 years of relevant work experience may be considered as an alternative to a degree
Applicants must have a current, active Government-Issued 8140 certification at IAT Level II or higher (such as Security+ CE, SecurityX, CCNA Security, CySA+ **, GICSP, GSEC, SSCP, CASP+ CE, CISSP, etc.) at the time of application, which is required to start. The candidate is responsible for maintaining their 8140 certifications throughout the entire contract period
Applicants must have a current, active in-scope Government-issued Top Secret/SCI security clearance at the time of application, which is required to start
This role requires rotating 24/7 shift work
Sound background and experience with operations and maintenance of large‑scale computer and communications systems/networking environments
Experience in system and/or network administration that includes UNIX, Linux, and Windows environments
Experience troubleshooting hardware and software components across complex, distributed systems
Experience with data flow usage and the ability to troubleshoot with internal and external agencies to establish and maintain network connectivity

Preferred Qualifications

Experience and knowledge of the C2BMC System or other Missile Defense Systems.
Linux certification (Linux Essentials, Linux+, LPIC‑1, RHCSA)
Experience using Confluence and Jira for documentation, tracking, and collaboration
Basic scripting experience (e.g., Bash) to automate routine tasks and support troubleshooting
Active Directory experience supporting account and group management in an enterprise environment

What We Can Offer You

Health Plan

Job Purpose

We make some of the UK’s best-known personal care brands in Leeds. Our Safety, Health & Environment (SHE) team keeps our people safe, protects our environment and keeps our site compliant. As our site becomes more data-led, we need sharper, faster ways to turn SHE information into clear insight and action. We’re looking for someone who loves data, problem-solving and making work simpler – and wants to use those skills for something that genuinely matters. You’ll build dashboards, automations and reports that help our leaders see where the real risks are, so we can spend less time chasing information and more time acting on the insights that make our operations safer for people and the environment.

Responsibilities

Build and maintain Power BI dashboards for safety, health and environmental performance
Automate the reporting that’s currently manual - using Power Automate, Power Apps, Forms and AI tools such as Copilot
Own the quality of our SHE data: collect it, check it, and make sure what we report is right, first time
Spot trends and outliers, explain what they mean, and help us decide where to focus next to improve SHE performance
Work with operations, engineering, finance and our global SHE teams to turn the data into action

All About You

What we’re looking for

Strong digital, analytical and data communication skills (or the appetite and evidence that you can get there fast)
Confidence working with imperfect data - cleaning, modelling and making it trustworthy
Curiosity about how a factory works and a genuine interest in health, safety and sustainability
A degree, apprenticeship or demonstrable self-taught capability in data, analytics or a related field

You don’t need

A SHE qualification – we’ll teach you the safety and environment side
Manufacturing experience – we’ll show you the factory floor

What You’ll Get

Real ownership from day one - this will be your remit, with the autonomy to build tools, improve processes and enable better data-led decisions
A development pathway into SHE, data or both, with exposure to global Unilever teams
A visible role with our site leadership team
The opportunity to work within a fantastic team at a world-class manufacturing facility

Interested but not sure you tick every box? Apply anyway – tell us what you’d automate first.

What We Offer

Not only do we offer a competitive salary and pension scheme, we also offer an annual bonus, subsidised gym membership, a discounted staff shop and shares. You’ll have the opportunity to work directly with our renowned and exciting brands in a flexible and hybrid working environment.

Whilst the role is advertised on a full-time basis, we would be happy to discuss possible flexible working options and what this may look like for you. We are a key advocate of wellbeing and offer a variety of support for our people including hubs, programmes and development opportunities. We strive to achieve a family-friendly and inclusive workplace and to, above all, create possibilities for all.

Diversity at Unilever is about inclusion, embracing differences, creating possibilities and growing together for better business performance. We embrace diversity in our workforce. This means giving full and fair consideration to all applicants and continuing development of all employees regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, race, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, marriage and civil partnership, and pregnancy and maternity. We are also more than happy to provide reasonable adjustments during our application and interview process to enable you to be present your best self. To find out more, including about our Employee Resource Groups, please click here Equity, Diversity & Inclusion at Unilever | Unilever.

Recruitment Fraud

Cyber criminals advertise fake job adverts with prestigious employers as a way of stealing information or even defrauding individuals out of money. In the most sophisticated cases, they will set up fake websites, which have a similar address to companies like Unilever. They even conduct fake telephone interviews and then offer candidates a role with the proviso they pay a fee for background checks or to cover work visa costs.  These types of attacks are becoming more common as more people are looking for employment in the economic climate.

How is Unilever tackling this?

Many of Unilever’s recruitment sites publish a warning to candidates about recruitment fraud. The Cyber Security team also proactively scan for signs of people setting up fake Unilever sites and act to close them down.

What can I do?

If you become aware of potential recruitment fraud, spot fake Unilever recruitment adverts or fake LinkedIn profiles, report them via Una Live Chat.

Unilever does not accept responsibility or liability for any candidates who are financially impacted by recruitment fraud. Your vigilance is key!

jobs.title: Sr. Project Manager - Environmental Remediation
jobs.description:
Position:
Sr. Project Manager - Environmental Remediation, Byram Township, NJ Posted:
06/10/2026

Summary Of Job Description

The Senior Project Manager (Sr. PM) assists CAPE in achieving strategic and business objectives by leading project management processes (initiation, planning, executing, monitoring/controlling, and closing) for projects across New Jersey. This Sr. PM role is responsible for both construction and environmental remediation delivery and must be capable of managing field execution, subcontractors, schedules, budgets, safety, quality, and federal documentation requirements.

The Sr. PM integrates all project management knowledge areas (scope, cost, time, quality, safety, resources, communications, risk, procurement, and stakeholder management) so the project functions as a cohesive whole. This position serves as a primary point of contact with clients and agencies and effectively leads teams of scientists, engineers, procurement specialists, subcontractors, field personnel, and other stakeholders to meet CAPE’s financial and performance goals.

This role is onsite at active project locations. Not a remote role.

Key Responsibilities

Lead onsite project execution to deliver scope safely, on schedule, and within budget; develop the execution approach, staffing plan, and phased work plan based on scope and risk.
Build and run the Project Management Plan (scope, schedule, cost, quality, safety, resources, communications, risk, procurement, and stakeholders) and keep plans/baselines current as changes occur.
Control scope using WBS/work packages; manage contract requirements, modifications, and change orders, including impact analysis and timely approvals.
Develop and maintain the integrated schedule (near-term planning through milestones); drive weekly/monthly reporting, corrective actions, and a monthly performance analysis/forecast.
Own project financial performance, cost control, forecasting (ETC/EAC), variance analysis, and recovery plans; identify cost drivers and correct excessive-cost items.
Embed safety and quality into planning and field execution; ensure Safety Plans are in place and followed; maintain incident reporting and a zero-incident culture.
Manage procurement and subcontractors, define and negotiate scopes, oversee performance and invoices, and ensure submittals and progress payments are processed accurately and on time.
Serve as primary client/agency interface (USACE/USEPA as applicable); communicate progress, risks, and issues to stakeholders and executive management; resolve disputes professionally and promptly.
Supervise and lead project staff in accordance with company policies and applicable laws; perform other duties as assigned.

Required Skills, Knowledge & Tools

Ability to read, analyze, and interpret technical procedures, engineering drawings/specifications, and applicable government regulations (including FAR familiarity).
Strong written and verbal communication skills—able to write clear reports/correspondence and confidently present project status, risks, and decisions to stakeholders.
Persuasive communicator with effective negotiation skills; able to develop strong working relationships with executive management, clients, and subcontractors.
Primavera P6 scheduling experience (required/strongly preferred).

Salary

Up to $160,000 annually, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

Travel

50 % on average

Minimum Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications (Project Manager II) – bachelor’s degree in engineering/science or construction management required. Must have at least three (3) years of progressively responsible related field experience and task management, and two (2) years of onsite Quality Control experience supporting environmental and/or infrastructure work. Must demonstrate a firm grasp of the key project management knowledge areas (scope, schedule, cost, quality, safety, risk, procurement, communications, stakeholders) as determined by management review.
Senior-Level Requirements (in addition to the above) – Minimum ten (10) years of successful project management experience with emphasis on cost, schedule, communications, and resource management on construction and/or environmental remediation projects. Must have a professional certification (PMP, PE, or PG) and a proven track record delivering complex work (including successfully managing at least two (2) projects over $5M). Must have (or be able to obtain) required field credentials including OSHA 30-Hour Construction and 40-hour HAZWOPER with current refreshers.
Tools / Scheduling – Proficient in Microsoft Office and Windows-based systems; strong ability to develop and maintain project schedules. Primavera P6 experience required (or strongly preferred, depending on your HR “required vs preferred” structure).

Preferred Qualifications

Field experience in construction or environmental projects.

WHY CAPE?

For 35 years, CAPE has delivered construction and environmental remediation solutions to governmental and private organizations nationwide. As a $100 M small business, we have Nationwide contracts with the USACE, USN and USAF totaling over $20 B in prime contract capacity. As a top 3 SB in our industry, our $12 B portfolio also includes unrestricted contracts where we compete against large businesses for task order awards. Most recently in the unrestricted area, CAPE won a $30 M + groundwater treatment plant construction project for the USACE in New Jersey. We routinely partner with other small and large businesses to provide better responsiveness in support of achieving our clients’ goals.

Our projects are high-profile environmental remediation projects involving cleanup of contaminated soil, groundwater, and sediment. The culture of our company is one of working together to achieve our clients’ objectives, company goals and employee’s professional goals and is succinctly and accurately defined as “We, Not Me” behavior. To ensure long-term, sustainable growth, we tailor our 3-year vision to be ahead of our industry in delivering our projects, align with our clients and team partners to improve our existing market share and develop new services to support smart growth.

CAPE offers competitive benefits including Medical/Dental/Vision insurance, life insurance, Vanguard retirement savings plan including both traditional and Roth 401(k) with up to 4% match and lowest in class fees, health savings account (HSA) with investment option, flexible spending account (FSA), paid annual leave, paid maternity/paternity leave, and tuition reimbursement. CAPE also offers staff several other voluntary benefits options, as well as the option to work from home.

CAPE is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. We invite all qualified applicants to apply to our open positions.

jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager — Partner GTM Systems & Technology
jobs.description:
Overview

Role Overview

Intuit is undergoing a major transformation to modernize, unify, and scale our global partner ecosystem. The Global Partner Program (GPP) is our unified GTM framework designed to standardize enrollment, tiering, commercial benefits, and support experiences for all partner tracks—including Accountants, Value-Added Resellers (VARs), Developers, and ISVs—under a single platform: the Intuit Partner Suite (IPS).

As the Technical Program Manager for Partner GTM Systems & Technology Roadmap, you will own the technical execution engine of this program. You will serve as the single operations interface into the data and systems engineering teams. Your mission is to translate high-level program strategies into robust technical specifications, maintain and author all Business Requirements Documents (BRDs), manage the prioritization of the system roadmap, and aggressively mitigate technical risks to ensure flawless rollouts.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Own the Technical Backlog & Roadmap: Drive the technical prioritization, sequencing, and delivery roadmap for the Intuit Partner Suite (PRM/Portal) and integrated GTM tools (Salesforce, DocuSign, Quickbase, and Varicent) in direct partnership with systems and engineering leaders.
Business Requirements (BRD) Authorship & Lifecycle: Author, update, and finalize comprehensive Business Requirements Documents (BRDs). You will translate complex partner strategies, multi-tier revenue share structures, lead registration/protection rules, and tier-aware support routing—into clear, implementation-ready logic for developers.
Single Operations Interface to VEP/Engineering: Act as the centralized point of contact for all technical requirements, unifying and streamlining communication channels to eliminate historical fragmentation between business, ops, and engineering.
Cross-Functional Requirements Gathering: Collaborate deeply with GPP Program Strategy to capture strategic intent, and PMO to map system dependencies, ensuring technical plans directly support GPP launch-readiness schedules.
Technical Risk & Blocker Mitigation: Identify, track, and resolve system constraints and delivery risks. Focus areas include resolving data residency/GDPR requirements for international markets (UK, Canada, Australia) and managing the technical transition of legacy partner data into the new platform.
System Validation & UAT Governance: Define the operational quality standards and “Definition of Done” for technical deliverables. Lead User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and system validation to ensure shipped platform features exactly match defined business policies before they go live to partners.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications & Experience

Systems Implementation Expertise: 6+ years of experience leading complex, large-scale systems implementations across CRM (Salesforce/SFDC), Partner Relationship Management (PRM) platforms, Billing/Commerce engines, or Enterprise Data Warehouses.
Exceptional Business Analysis (BRD Writing): A proven track record of writing exceptionally detailed, logic-driven Business Requirements Documents (BRDs) that govern complex automation (e.g., tiered point accruals, referral payouts, and API-driven data integrations).
Technical Translator: Exceptional capability to bridge the gap between abstract business strategy and core engineering requirements, comfortably negotiating scope and trade-offs with both Executive Directors and System Architects.
Cross-Functional Collaborator: Experience navigating highly matrixed enterprise organizations, with a demonstrated ability to align diverse stakeholder groups (Sales, Ops, Product, Success, Finance, and Legal).
Detail-Oriented & Risk-Aware: High analytical rigor with experience using structured risk-management frameworks to identify operational constraints, system bugs, and process inefficiencies before they impact launch milestones.
Agile/Scrum Experience: Strong familiarity with Agile delivery methodologies, backlog grooming, and Jira-based sprint management.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with PRM tools (e.g., Salesforce PRM, Impartner, ZiftONE).
Familiarity with financial incentive systems (e.g., Varicent or automated revenue share platforms).
Direct experience working within B2B SaaS partner programs, channel operations, or agency reseller ecosystems.

Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

jobs.title: AI/Bio Research Project Manager, Operations (Term)
jobs.description:
Job Type

Term (Fixed Term)

RAND Center on AI, Security, and Technology (CAST)

About RAND

RAND is a nonprofit, nonpartisan research institution founded in 1948 to advise the U.S. government on matters of national security. For over 75 years, RAND has been a trusted source of objective, rigorous analysis for policymakers across administrations and agencies.

About CAST

CAST is an 80+ person center at the forefront of transformative AI and biotechnology policy and their implications for global competition and security. Our teams work on verification frameworks for international agreements on AI, creating AI data centers that are secure, unlocking energy for AI production, developing models for public-private partnerships between frontier labs and government, and conducting AIxBio evaluations and mitigations, among other initiatives.

Position Description

RAND Center on AI, Security, and Technology (CAST) is seeking an Operations Manager to support the Center’s people operations and management of the CAST Operations team. This is a high-ownership role on a fast-moving team supporting one of RAND's highest-priority research centers.

In this position, you will play a vital connective role across the organization. You’ll be an integral part of our operations team, enable our research teams to do their best work, and shape the experience of working at RAND CAST. This role blends hands-on operational execution with people-leadership and project-management responsibilities.

If you are someone who takes pride in making complex systems feel effortless, loves building environments where people thrive, and finds deep satisfaction in high impact work, this role is designed for you.

Responsibilities

People & Research Operations

Manage Center people support processes ensuring all new hires and exiting team members have a seamless, high-quality experience
Manage team members on fellowships, IPAs, and other deployments
Lead project management for internal team and RAND performance review cycles
Provide exceptional high-level project management on cross-center initiatives
Oversee the management of at least one satellite office

Operations Management

Serve as team lead for junior operations staff, providing mentorship, prioritization support, and day-to-day guidance
Identify and implement improvements to operational processes and systems
Partner with the Senior Operations Leads on sensitive and confidential matters, exercising strong discretion and judgment
Provide operations support across finance, procurement, events, communications, and cross-functional coordination
Build and maintain strong working relationships across research teams, central RAND functions, and external partners
Take on additional responsibilities as the Center's needs evolve

Qualifications

Required:

Experience managing teams of at least 2-3 people.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail; able to manage multiple time-sensitive processes simultaneously.
Experience navigating complex institutional structures and cross-functional partnerships.
Exceptionally clear and diplomatic communicator who maintains professionalism in all workplace interactions.
Ability to maintain composure and sound judgment under competing deadlines.

Preferred

Background in AI security, national security, or biosecurity.
Self-directed and proactive in identifying process improvements.

Education Requirements  

Minimum: Bachelor's degree; Master's degree preferred. A Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification can substitute for a Bachelor’s degree.  

Experience

jobs.title: Marketplace Business Operations Program Manager
jobs.description:
Collectors is the leading creator of innovative technology that provides value-added services for collectors worldwide. We grade, authenticate, vault, and sell millions of record-setting collectibles, all while modernizing and digitalizing the process to further our mission of helping collectors pursue their passions. We’re always on the lookout for talented people to join our growing team.

Our services span collectible trading cards, autographs, comic books, coins, video games, event tickets, and memorabilia. Our subsidiaries include PSA, PCGS, Beckett, SGC, and Card Ladder.

Since our founding in 1986, we have graded and authenticated millions of items. We employ more than 3000 people across our headquarters in Santa Ana, California and offices in New Jersey, Texas, Florida, Japan, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Canada, Mexico, Germany, the UK, and France.

As part of our interview process, we request that candidates have their cameras on during video interviews. This helps foster meaningful conversation and allows us to create an experience that closely resembles our standard working environment. Certain interview steps may take place by phone. For remote roles, and at our discretion, candidates may be asked to participate in an on-site interview as part of the final stages of the process.

We understand there may be occasional circumstances requiring accommodation and are happy to discuss them as needed. Your recruiter will be able to clarify expectations and answer any questions you have.

Marketplace is a new organization at Collectors, including PSA Exchange and eBay consignment. We’re looking for an experienced generalist to join our team as a Marketplace Business Operations Program Manager
. You’ll oversee critical day-to-day functions and strategic project delivery, ensuring that business critical initiatives are executed efficiently and accurately. You will cover a wide range of projects across all of our business lines and functions. This is a high growth potential role, with a variety of pathways for advancement.

You’ll report to the Sr. Manager, Marketplace and work from our Santa Ana, CA or Jersey City, NJ office (with preference to candidates who can work from our Jersey City, NJ office).
Remote or hybrid candidates will also be considered. We believe that there is significant value in in-person collaboration. If you live within a 1 hour commuting distance to one of our offices, you will be required to be onsite most of the time. This will be discussed further as part of the recruiting process.

What You’ll Do

Manage operational functions key to the day-to-day running of the business
Enable our next phase of growth by building scalable systems to replace manual processes
Execute larger scale business transformation projects from start to finish in a highly organized fashion
Partner with other functional teams within our business to set up operational rigor and strong cadences to solve their operating challenges
Manage bespoke billing and fulfillment programs for key accounts as necessary
Leverage AI and other tools to build automation into our processes wherever possible

Who You Are

5+ years of experience in marketplace / e-commerce business operations, strategy, or program management OR 3+ years of management consulting
Generalist approach with a willingness to tackle a wide variety of projects
Highly organized and detail oriented with a strong internal sense of urgency
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; comfortable using data to drive decisions.
Excellent project management, communication, and cross-functional collaboration abilities.

Salary Range

The salary range for this position is $110,000-$180,000. Actual compensation on this range varies based on a variety of non-discriminatory factors, including location, job level, experience, and skill set. This role may be eligible for bonuses, commissions, or other forms of compensation, please ask your recruiter for details.

Health Insurance: All full-time employees are eligible to enroll in Medical, Dental, and Vision

Holiday Pay: All regular, full-time employees are eligible for ten company paid holidays
Employee Discounts: Employees receive discounts on select grading services for approved submissions
Flexible Hours: Many of our teams offer flexible schedules with varying shifts and will work with you to accommodate your needs
Fun Working Environment: Our team members are invited to participate in celebrations, holiday events, and team building activities

jobs.title: Clean Energy Senior Project Manager
jobs.description:
Join the Clean Energy Revolution

Become a Clean Energy Senior Project Manager
at Southern California Edison (SCE) and build a better tomorrow. In this job, you will work in the Clean Energy Project Management (CRPM) group within Project and Program Management, responsible for leading projects through design construction for light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicle customers requesting service throughout the SCE territory. As the Electric Vehicle (EV) market continues to grow, light, medium, and heavy-duty EV customers continue to increase their footprint requesting new services or expansion of their existing services, and require customer focus and support of their projects.

Transportation Electrification (TE) is a critical strategic initiative for Southern California Edison (SCE) and we are taking a leading role to ensure that TE plays a major part in the reduction of greenhouse gas (GHG) and criteria pollutant emissions in California. The transportation sector is one of the largest consumers of energy, second to electric power generation, with the majority of energy consumed coming from petroleum.

Electrifying the transportation sector and reducing petroleum usage is critical to realizing California's ambitious climate and air quality goals. In addition to cleaning and modernizing the grid, SCE is offering tariffs to support charger availability, make electric fueling more affordable and increase awareness of the benefits of electric transportation.

As a Clean Energy Senior Project Manager
, your work will help power our planet, reduce carbon emissions and create cleaner air for everyone. Are you ready to take on the challenge to help us build the future?

Responsibilities

Manages high impact, strategic projects effectively using project management principles, tools, and techniques under time constraints, shifting priorities, and making critical decisions, providing direction to supporting team members.
Directs project initiation, planning, execution, control, and closure for core disciplines of project management (scope, schedule, and budget) independently and provides guidance/mentorship to subordinate Project Managers/Associate Project Managers.
Leads moderate to highly complex projects and delivers on strategic objectives by influencing stakeholders across multiple departments and exercising independent decision making, with limited consultation from leadership.
Collaborates with Project Managers, department/division senior and executive leadership, and other stakeholders internal and external to the company as a key consultant to provide recommendation and make critical decisions that that have broad impacts across multiple organizations.
Manages planning, development, and/or execution of electric transmission/distribution projects, which may include but is not limited to, wildfire, infrastructure replacement, load growth, poles, line upgrades, maintenance, or installations.
Drives milestones and reports on large transmission and/or distribution projects which may include designs, schedules, projects applications, compliance and safety documentation, regulatory filings, and local and state agency coordination.
Leads technical standards, specifications, and architecture that optimize system reliability, efficiency, capacity, resilience, and asset management.
Oversees technology integration efforts including new SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) systems, digital substations, automation, and advanced grid analytics platforms.
A material job duty of all positions within the Company is ensuring the protection of all its physical, financial and cybersecurity assets, and properly accessing and managing private customer data, proprietary information, confidential medical records, and other types of highly sensitive information and data with the highest standards of conduct and integrity.

Minimum Qualifications

Ten or more years of experience in project management.

Preferred Qualifications

Proven experience in project management delivery of scope, schedule, and budget commitments while overseeing full IPSEC scope (Initiation, Planning, Scheduling, Executing, and Closing).
Bachelor's degree in business, engineering, project construction management, or a related field; PMP credential preferred. Ability to integrate work across relevant areas, lead risks and safety appropriately, develop and execute business plans, manage information, and provide outstanding service to internal and external customers.
Experience managing multiple high-impact projects with tight timelines and various stakeholders with demonstrated proficiency in resource and project planning, decision making, and results delivery.
Exceptional business analytics and problem-solving skills to drive data-driven decision-making.
Effective communication with an adaptive style to collaborate effectively with clients, residents, cross-functional teams and stakeholders.
Strong time-management skills with the ability to organize and proactively prioritize a large volume of projects simultaneously.
Strong ethics, influence and negotiation, leadership, interpersonal skills, communication, and the ability to effectively handle stress and engage in continuous learning.
Experience mentoring co-workers, providing small team leadership, delivering on-going training as needed for peers and support personnel.
Advanced experience using Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook with proficiency using Design Manager (DM), Click, and SAP.

Additional Information

This position’s work mode is hybrid. The employee will report to an SCE facility for a set number of days with the option to work remotely on the remaining days. Unless otherwise noted, employees are required to work and reside in the state of California. Further details of this work mode will be discussed at the interview stage. The work mode can be changed based on business needs.
Visit our Candidate Resource page to get meaningful information related to benefits, perks, resources, testing information, hiring process, and more!
Qualified applications with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act.
The primary work location for this position is Pomona, CA.
Position will require up to 30% traveling and being out in the field throughout the SCE service territory.
Relocation does not apply to this position

About Southern California Edison

The people at SCE don't just keep the lights on. Our mission is so much bigger. We’re fueling the kind of innovation that’s changing an entire industry, and quite possibly the planet. Join us and create a future with cleaner energy, while providing our customers with the safety and reliability they demand. At SCE, you’ll have a chance to grow personally and professionally, making a real impact in Southern California and around the world.

Southern California Edison is a proud Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability and protected veteran status.

We are committed to ensuring that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment.
