new_jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager — Partner GTM Systems & Technology
new_jobs.description:
Overview

Role Overview

Intuit is undergoing a major transformation to modernize, unify, and scale our global partner ecosystem. The Global Partner Program (GPP) is our unified GTM framework designed to standardize enrollment, tiering, commercial benefits, and support experiences for all partner tracks—including Accountants, Value-Added Resellers (VARs), Developers, and ISVs—under a single platform: the Intuit Partner Suite (IPS).

As the Technical Program Manager for Partner GTM Systems & Technology Roadmap, you will own the technical execution engine of this program. You will serve as the single operations interface into the data and systems engineering teams. Your mission is to translate high-level program strategies into robust technical specifications, maintain and author all Business Requirements Documents (BRDs), manage the prioritization of the system roadmap, and aggressively mitigate technical risks to ensure flawless rollouts.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Own the Technical Backlog & Roadmap: Drive the technical prioritization, sequencing, and delivery roadmap for the Intuit Partner Suite (PRM/Portal) and integrated GTM tools (Salesforce, DocuSign, Quickbase, and Varicent) in direct partnership with systems and engineering leaders.
Business Requirements (BRD) Authorship & Lifecycle: Author, update, and finalize comprehensive Business Requirements Documents (BRDs). You will translate complex partner strategies, multi-tier revenue share structures, lead registration/protection rules, and tier-aware support routing—into clear, implementation-ready logic for developers.
Single Operations Interface to VEP/Engineering: Act as the centralized point of contact for all technical requirements, unifying and streamlining communication channels to eliminate historical fragmentation between business, ops, and engineering.
Cross-Functional Requirements Gathering: Collaborate deeply with GPP Program Strategy to capture strategic intent, and PMO to map system dependencies, ensuring technical plans directly support GPP launch-readiness schedules.
Technical Risk & Blocker Mitigation: Identify, track, and resolve system constraints and delivery risks. Focus areas include resolving data residency/GDPR requirements for international markets (UK, Canada, Australia) and managing the technical transition of legacy partner data into the new platform.
System Validation & UAT Governance: Define the operational quality standards and “Definition of Done” for technical deliverables. Lead User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and system validation to ensure shipped platform features exactly match defined business policies before they go live to partners.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications & Experience

Systems Implementation Expertise: 6+ years of experience leading complex, large-scale systems implementations across CRM (Salesforce/SFDC), Partner Relationship Management (PRM) platforms, Billing/Commerce engines, or Enterprise Data Warehouses.
Exceptional Business Analysis (BRD Writing): A proven track record of writing exceptionally detailed, logic-driven Business Requirements Documents (BRDs) that govern complex automation (e.g., tiered point accruals, referral payouts, and API-driven data integrations).
Technical Translator: Exceptional capability to bridge the gap between abstract business strategy and core engineering requirements, comfortably negotiating scope and trade-offs with both Executive Directors and System Architects.
Cross-Functional Collaborator: Experience navigating highly matrixed enterprise organizations, with a demonstrated ability to align diverse stakeholder groups (Sales, Ops, Product, Success, Finance, and Legal).
Detail-Oriented & Risk-Aware: High analytical rigor with experience using structured risk-management frameworks to identify operational constraints, system bugs, and process inefficiencies before they impact launch milestones.
Agile/Scrum Experience: Strong familiarity with Agile delivery methodologies, backlog grooming, and Jira-based sprint management.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with PRM tools (e.g., Salesforce PRM, Impartner, ZiftONE).
Familiarity with financial incentive systems (e.g., Varicent or automated revenue share platforms).
Direct experience working within B2B SaaS partner programs, channel operations, or agency reseller ecosystems.

Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

new_jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager — Partner GTM Systems & Technology
new_jobs.description:
Overview

Role Overview

Intuit is undergoing a major transformation to modernize, unify, and scale our global partner ecosystem. The Global Partner Program (GPP) is our unified GTM framework designed to standardize enrollment, tiering, commercial benefits, and support experiences for all partner tracks—including Accountants, Value-Added Resellers (VARs), Developers, and ISVs—under a single platform: the Intuit Partner Suite (IPS).

As the Technical Program Manager for Partner GTM Systems & Technology Roadmap, you will own the technical execution engine of this program. You will serve as the single operations interface into the data and systems engineering teams. Your mission is to translate high-level program strategies into robust technical specifications, maintain and author all Business Requirements Documents (BRDs), manage the prioritization of the system roadmap, and aggressively mitigate technical risks to ensure flawless rollouts.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Own the Technical Backlog & Roadmap: Drive the technical prioritization, sequencing, and delivery roadmap for the Intuit Partner Suite (PRM/Portal) and integrated GTM tools (Salesforce, DocuSign, Quickbase, and Varicent) in direct partnership with systems and engineering leaders.
Business Requirements (BRD) Authorship & Lifecycle: Author, update, and finalize comprehensive Business Requirements Documents (BRDs). You will translate complex partner strategies, multi-tier revenue share structures, lead registration/protection rules, and tier-aware support routing—into clear, implementation-ready logic for developers.
Single Operations Interface to VEP/Engineering: Act as the centralized point of contact for all technical requirements, unifying and streamlining communication channels to eliminate historical fragmentation between business, ops, and engineering.
Cross-Functional Requirements Gathering: Collaborate deeply with GPP Program Strategy to capture strategic intent, and PMO to map system dependencies, ensuring technical plans directly support GPP launch-readiness schedules.
Technical Risk & Blocker Mitigation: Identify, track, and resolve system constraints and delivery risks. Focus areas include resolving data residency/GDPR requirements for international markets (UK, Canada, Australia) and managing the technical transition of legacy partner data into the new platform.
System Validation & UAT Governance: Define the operational quality standards and “Definition of Done” for technical deliverables. Lead User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and system validation to ensure shipped platform features exactly match defined business policies before they go live to partners.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications & Experience

Systems Implementation Expertise: 6+ years of experience leading complex, large-scale systems implementations across CRM (Salesforce/SFDC), Partner Relationship Management (PRM) platforms, Billing/Commerce engines, or Enterprise Data Warehouses.
Exceptional Business Analysis (BRD Writing): A proven track record of writing exceptionally detailed, logic-driven Business Requirements Documents (BRDs) that govern complex automation (e.g., tiered point accruals, referral payouts, and API-driven data integrations).
Technical Translator: Exceptional capability to bridge the gap between abstract business strategy and core engineering requirements, comfortably negotiating scope and trade-offs with both Executive Directors and System Architects.
Cross-Functional Collaborator: Experience navigating highly matrixed enterprise organizations, with a demonstrated ability to align diverse stakeholder groups (Sales, Ops, Product, Success, Finance, and Legal).
Detail-Oriented & Risk-Aware: High analytical rigor with experience using structured risk-management frameworks to identify operational constraints, system bugs, and process inefficiencies before they impact launch milestones.
Agile/Scrum Experience: Strong familiarity with Agile delivery methodologies, backlog grooming, and Jira-based sprint management.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with PRM tools (e.g., Salesforce PRM, Impartner, ZiftONE).
Familiarity with financial incentive systems (e.g., Varicent or automated revenue share platforms).
Direct experience working within B2B SaaS partner programs, channel operations, or agency reseller ecosystems.

Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

new_jobs.description:
Job Type

Term (Fixed Term)

RAND Center on AI, Security, and Technology (CAST)

About RAND

RAND is a nonprofit, nonpartisan research institution founded in 1948 to advise the U.S. government on matters of national security. For over 75 years, RAND has been a trusted source of objective, rigorous analysis for policymakers across administrations and agencies.

About CAST

CAST is an 80+ person center at the forefront of transformative AI and biotechnology policy and their implications for global competition and security. Our teams work on verification frameworks for international agreements on AI, creating AI data centers that are secure, unlocking energy for AI production, developing models for public-private partnerships between frontier labs and government, and conducting AIxBio evaluations and mitigations, among other initiatives.

Position Description

RAND Center on AI, Security, and Technology (CAST) is seeking an Operations Manager to support the Center’s people operations and management of the CAST Operations team. This is a high-ownership role on a fast-moving team supporting one of RAND's highest-priority research centers.

In this position, you will play a vital connective role across the organization. You’ll be an integral part of our operations team, enable our research teams to do their best work, and shape the experience of working at RAND CAST. This role blends hands-on operational execution with people-leadership and project-management responsibilities.

If you are someone who takes pride in making complex systems feel effortless, loves building environments where people thrive, and finds deep satisfaction in high impact work, this role is designed for you.

Responsibilities

People & Research Operations

Manage Center people support processes ensuring all new hires and exiting team members have a seamless, high-quality experience
Manage team members on fellowships, IPAs, and other deployments
Lead project management for internal team and RAND performance review cycles
Provide exceptional high-level project management on cross-center initiatives
Oversee the management of at least one satellite office

Operations Management

Serve as team lead for junior operations staff, providing mentorship, prioritization support, and day-to-day guidance
Identify and implement improvements to operational processes and systems
Partner with the Senior Operations Leads on sensitive and confidential matters, exercising strong discretion and judgment
Provide operations support across finance, procurement, events, communications, and cross-functional coordination
Build and maintain strong working relationships across research teams, central RAND functions, and external partners
Take on additional responsibilities as the Center's needs evolve

Qualifications

Required:

Experience managing teams of at least 2-3 people.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail; able to manage multiple time-sensitive processes simultaneously.
Experience navigating complex institutional structures and cross-functional partnerships.
Exceptionally clear and diplomatic communicator who maintains professionalism in all workplace interactions.
Ability to maintain composure and sound judgment under competing deadlines.

Preferred

Background in AI security, national security, or biosecurity.
Self-directed and proactive in identifying process improvements.

Education Requirements  

Minimum: Bachelor's degree; Master's degree preferred. A Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification can substitute for a Bachelor’s degree.  

Experience  

8 years minimum experience; 10 years preferred.  

Security Clearance  

Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government clearance is preferred but not required.  

Term 

This position is a 3-year term appointment with a possibility of renewal, alongside options for longer term employment. We are seeking full-time candidates.  

Location  

Washington, DC (preferred); Santa Monica, CA; Pittsburgh, PA; or Boston, MA. Hybrid work arrangement, combining work from home and on-site options in these locations.  

Salary Range:
$102,800 - $174,400

new_jobs.title: Marketplace Business Operations Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Collectors is the leading creator of innovative technology that provides value-added services for collectors worldwide. We grade, authenticate, vault, and sell millions of record-setting collectibles, all while modernizing and digitalizing the process to further our mission of helping collectors pursue their passions. We’re always on the lookout for talented people to join our growing team.

Our services span collectible trading cards, autographs, comic books, coins, video games, event tickets, and memorabilia. Our subsidiaries include PSA, PCGS, Beckett, SGC, and Card Ladder.

Since our founding in 1986, we have graded and authenticated millions of items. We employ more than 3000 people across our headquarters in Santa Ana, California and offices in New Jersey, Texas, Florida, Japan, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Canada, Mexico, Germany, the UK, and France.

As part of our interview process, we request that candidates have their cameras on during video interviews. This helps foster meaningful conversation and allows us to create an experience that closely resembles our standard working environment. Certain interview steps may take place by phone. For remote roles, and at our discretion, candidates may be asked to participate in an on-site interview as part of the final stages of the process.

We understand there may be occasional circumstances requiring accommodation and are happy to discuss them as needed. Your recruiter will be able to clarify expectations and answer any questions you have.

Marketplace is a new organization at Collectors, including PSA Exchange and eBay consignment. We’re looking for an experienced generalist to join our team as a Marketplace Business Operations Program Manager
. You’ll oversee critical day-to-day functions and strategic project delivery, ensuring that business critical initiatives are executed efficiently and accurately. You will cover a wide range of projects across all of our business lines and functions. This is a high growth potential role, with a variety of pathways for advancement.

You’ll report to the Sr. Manager, Marketplace and work from our Santa Ana, CA or Jersey City, NJ office (with preference to candidates who can work from our Jersey City, NJ office).
Remote or hybrid candidates will also be considered. We believe that there is significant value in in-person collaboration. If you live within a 1 hour commuting distance to one of our offices, you will be required to be onsite most of the time. This will be discussed further as part of the recruiting process.

What You’ll Do

Manage operational functions key to the day-to-day running of the business
Enable our next phase of growth by building scalable systems to replace manual processes
Execute larger scale business transformation projects from start to finish in a highly organized fashion
Partner with other functional teams within our business to set up operational rigor and strong cadences to solve their operating challenges
Manage bespoke billing and fulfillment programs for key accounts as necessary
Leverage AI and other tools to build automation into our processes wherever possible

Who You Are

5+ years of experience in marketplace / e-commerce business operations, strategy, or program management OR 3+ years of management consulting
Generalist approach with a willingness to tackle a wide variety of projects
Highly organized and detail oriented with a strong internal sense of urgency
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; comfortable using data to drive decisions.
Excellent project management, communication, and cross-functional collaboration abilities.

Salary Range

The salary range for this position is $110,000-$180,000. Actual compensation on this range varies based on a variety of non-discriminatory factors, including location, job level, experience, and skill set. This role may be eligible for bonuses, commissions, or other forms of compensation, please ask your recruiter for details.

Reasons To Join Us

Health Insurance: All full-time employees are eligible to enroll in Medical, Dental, and Vision
Additional Benefits: Full-time employees are eligible for fertility, commuter, and educational assistance benefits
401(K) Matching Plan: We are proud to offer a competitive 401k matching plan to our employees to support their future financial goals
Vacation: All salaried employees are eligible for flexible time-off
Holiday Pay: All regular, full-time employees are eligible for ten company paid holidays
Employee Discounts: Employees receive discounts on select grading services for approved submissions
Flexible Hours: Many of our teams offer flexible schedules with varying shifts and will work with you to accommodate your needs
Fun Working Environment: Our team members are invited to participate in celebrations, holiday events, and team building activities

Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States.

#BI-Hybrid #BI-Remote

new_jobs.title: Clean Energy Senior Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Join the Clean Energy Revolution

Become a Clean Energy Senior Project Manager
at Southern California Edison (SCE) and build a better tomorrow. In this job, you will work in the Clean Energy Project Management (CRPM) group within Project and Program Management, responsible for leading projects through design construction for light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicle customers requesting service throughout the SCE territory. As the Electric Vehicle (EV) market continues to grow, light, medium, and heavy-duty EV customers continue to increase their footprint requesting new services or expansion of their existing services, and require customer focus and support of their projects.

Transportation Electrification (TE) is a critical strategic initiative for Southern California Edison (SCE) and we are taking a leading role to ensure that TE plays a major part in the reduction of greenhouse gas (GHG) and criteria pollutant emissions in California. The transportation sector is one of the largest consumers of energy, second to electric power generation, with the majority of energy consumed coming from petroleum.

Electrifying the transportation sector and reducing petroleum usage is critical to realizing California's ambitious climate and air quality goals. In addition to cleaning and modernizing the grid, SCE is offering tariffs to support charger availability, make electric fueling more affordable and increase awareness of the benefits of electric transportation.

As a Clean Energy Senior Project Manager
, your work will help power our planet, reduce carbon emissions and create cleaner air for everyone. Are you ready to take on the challenge to help us build the future?

Responsibilities

Manages high impact, strategic projects effectively using project management principles, tools, and techniques under time constraints, shifting priorities, and making critical decisions, providing direction to supporting team members.
Directs project initiation, planning, execution, control, and closure for core disciplines of project management (scope, schedule, and budget) independently and provides guidance/mentorship to subordinate Project Managers/Associate Project Managers.
Leads moderate to highly complex projects and delivers on strategic objectives by influencing stakeholders across multiple departments and exercising independent decision making, with limited consultation from leadership.
Collaborates with Project Managers, department/division senior and executive leadership, and other stakeholders internal and external to the company as a key consultant to provide recommendation and make critical decisions that that have broad impacts across multiple organizations.
Manages planning, development, and/or execution of electric transmission/distribution projects, which may include but is not limited to, wildfire, infrastructure replacement, load growth, poles, line upgrades, maintenance, or installations.
Drives milestones and reports on large transmission and/or distribution projects which may include designs, schedules, projects applications, compliance and safety documentation, regulatory filings, and local and state agency coordination.
Leads technical standards, specifications, and architecture that optimize system reliability, efficiency, capacity, resilience, and asset management.
Oversees technology integration efforts including new SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) systems, digital substations, automation, and advanced grid analytics platforms.
A material job duty of all positions within the Company is ensuring the protection of all its physical, financial and cybersecurity assets, and properly accessing and managing private customer data, proprietary information, confidential medical records, and other types of highly sensitive information and data with the highest standards of conduct and integrity.

Minimum Qualifications

Ten or more years of experience in project management.

Preferred Qualifications

Proven experience in project management delivery of scope, schedule, and budget commitments while overseeing full IPSEC scope (Initiation, Planning, Scheduling, Executing, and Closing).
Bachelor's degree in business, engineering, project construction management, or a related field; PMP credential preferred. Ability to integrate work across relevant areas, lead risks and safety appropriately, develop and execute business plans, manage information, and provide outstanding service to internal and external customers.
Experience managing multiple high-impact projects with tight timelines and various stakeholders with demonstrated proficiency in resource and project planning, decision making, and results delivery.
Exceptional business analytics and problem-solving skills to drive data-driven decision-making.
Effective communication with an adaptive style to collaborate effectively with clients, residents, cross-functional teams and stakeholders.
Strong time-management skills with the ability to organize and proactively prioritize a large volume of projects simultaneously.
Strong ethics, influence and negotiation, leadership, interpersonal skills, communication, and the ability to effectively handle stress and engage in continuous learning.
Experience mentoring co-workers, providing small team leadership, delivering on-going training as needed for peers and support personnel.
Advanced experience using Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook with proficiency using Design Manager (DM), Click, and SAP.

Additional Information

This position’s work mode is hybrid. The employee will report to an SCE facility for a set number of days with the option to work remotely on the remaining days. Unless otherwise noted, employees are required to work and reside in the state of California. Further details of this work mode will be discussed at the interview stage. The work mode can be changed based on business needs.
Visit our Candidate Resource page to get meaningful information related to benefits, perks, resources, testing information, hiring process, and more!
Qualified applications with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act.
The primary work location for this position is Pomona, CA.
Position will require up to 30% traveling and being out in the field throughout the SCE service territory.
Relocation does not apply to this position

About Southern California Edison

The people at SCE don't just keep the lights on. Our mission is so much bigger. We’re fueling the kind of innovation that’s changing an entire industry, and quite possibly the planet. Join us and create a future with cleaner energy, while providing our customers with the safety and reliability they demand. At SCE, you’ll have a chance to grow personally and professionally, making a real impact in Southern California and around the world.

NG Space Systems is looking for a Manager, Program Level 3, to provide leadership to the Program Management organization for the Propulsion portfolio supporting the Mission Enabling Products (MEP) Business Unit in the fast-growing Intelligence Systems Division (ISD) in Commerce, California.

This position is 100% On-Site

(MEP) is a leading designer, producer, and supplier of spacecraft components that power and enable satellites of all classes. Products include spacecraft panels, bus structures, precision optical structures, deployable structural systems and mechanisms, solar arrays, antenna reflectors and propulsion tanks. Our products are on virtually every U.S. satellite built in the last 20 years.

Learn more about Mission Enabling Products at our website: https://www.northropgrumman.com/space/spacecraft-components

Overview

The selected candidate will report to the Propulsion Product Director and serve as a key member of the leadership team for the evolving Propulsion portfolio. The candidate selected will be involved in program execution, cost, schedule, staffing, team building, customer satisfaction, ensuring compliance with organizational processes and procedures, maintaining relationships with and providing status to program leadership and customers. The individual will lead a matrixed-functional team aligned to common program performance goals from inception of an idea through program completion.

As a program manager, the primary objective will be the delivery of all contractual requirements on cost and schedule, while achieving all technical objectives and creating customer intimacy to support value creation strategies and actions. Program Managers are responsible for leading all phases of the program life cycle from inception (proposal development) through startup, execution, and completion (contract closeout). The individual will lead a cross-functional organization aligned to common program performance goals.

The candidate will be responsible for technical leadership and functional management of the Propulsion Program Managers. The candidate must be able to effectively communicate complex concepts, have a successful track record of program performance, and possess interpersonal team building skills. The selected candidate for this position must work full-time, on-site at the Northrop Grumman Commerce, CA site.

Role And Responsibilities

Besides functional responsibilities, primary program responsibilities are the management of cost, schedule, and technical performance of company programs and include, but are not limited to, the following:

Set vision, lead, and manage an ~8-person team of program managers
Functional management of Program Manager team (time reporting, performance reviews, statement of work, performance evaluations, employee development, mentoring efforts, engagements, and other functional tasks)
Demonstrate a commitment to ethics and integrity, and the capability to innovate while challenging traditional ways of doing business
Interface directly with the Customer, Business Management, Contracts, Engineering, and other functional/support teams in support of program objectives, technical integrity, customer expectations, and schedule
Develop and implement team structures, organizational framework, and processes to optimize productivity and foster a high-performing, cohesive, and collaborative team environment
Developing new business opportunities through long term strategic planning, capture planning, and development of proposals and business plans
Identify, allocate, and manage program resources, including workforce planning
Adhere to all internal processes, policies, and applicable industry standards
Manage proposals, negotiation of contracts, contract changes, specifications, operating budgets, schedule milestones, and key terms and conditions
Cultivate customer relationships and intimacy to develop further opportunities within the customer community
Establish a program organization that effectively addresses customer requirements and incorporates the necessary internal and external sub-organizations
Establish design concepts, criteria, and engineering efforts for product research, development, and integration and test
Conduct thorough risk & opportunity management
Lead and direct cross-functional Integrated Program Teams (IPT) to meet program cost, schedule and technical performance objectives
Ensure the program team understands and adheres to contract scope, and implements changes through a control board

new_jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager — Partner GTM Systems & Technology
new_jobs.description:
Overview

Role Overview

Intuit is undergoing a major transformation to modernize, unify, and scale our global partner ecosystem. The Global Partner Program (GPP) is our unified GTM framework designed to standardize enrollment, tiering, commercial benefits, and support experiences for all partner tracks—including Accountants, Value-Added Resellers (VARs), Developers, and ISVs—under a single platform: the Intuit Partner Suite (IPS).

As the Technical Program Manager for Partner GTM Systems & Technology Roadmap, you will own the technical execution engine of this program. You will serve as the single operations interface into the data and systems engineering teams. Your mission is to translate high-level program strategies into robust technical specifications, maintain and author all Business Requirements Documents (BRDs), manage the prioritization of the system roadmap, and aggressively mitigate technical risks to ensure flawless rollouts.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Own the Technical Backlog & Roadmap: Drive the technical prioritization, sequencing, and delivery roadmap for the Intuit Partner Suite (PRM/Portal) and integrated GTM tools (Salesforce, DocuSign, Quickbase, and Varicent) in direct partnership with systems and engineering leaders.
Business Requirements (BRD) Authorship & Lifecycle: Author, update, and finalize comprehensive Business Requirements Documents (BRDs). You will translate complex partner strategies, multi-tier revenue share structures, lead registration/protection rules, and tier-aware support routing—into clear, implementation-ready logic for developers.
Single Operations Interface to VEP/Engineering: Act as the centralized point of contact for all technical requirements, unifying and streamlining communication channels to eliminate historical fragmentation between business, ops, and engineering.
Cross-Functional Requirements Gathering: Collaborate deeply with GPP Program Strategy to capture strategic intent, and PMO to map system dependencies, ensuring technical plans directly support GPP launch-readiness schedules.
Technical Risk & Blocker Mitigation: Identify, track, and resolve system constraints and delivery risks. Focus areas include resolving data residency/GDPR requirements for international markets (UK, Canada, Australia) and managing the technical transition of legacy partner data into the new platform.
System Validation & UAT Governance: Define the operational quality standards and “Definition of Done” for technical deliverables. Lead User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and system validation to ensure shipped platform features exactly match defined business policies before they go live to partners.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications & Experience

new_jobs.description:
About The Team

The Industrial Security team enables OpenAI’s classified and national security work by building secure, compliant programs that support government customers and protect sensitive information. We partner across Security, Legal, People, Facilities, Engineering, IT, and program leadership to translate complex government requirements into practical operating models that allow important work to move forward responsibly. Our work spans personnel security, classified facilities, special programs, government customer engagement, and the safeguards required to operate in highly regulated environments.

About The Role

As a Senior Special Programs Security Manager, you will lead security operations for OpenAI’s Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) and Special Access Programs (SAP), serving in customer-designated roles such as Contractor Special Security Officer (CSSO) or Contractor Program Security Officer (CPSO). You will help shape how OpenAI operates across the Intelligence Community and other national security environments, building the relationships, processes, and security foundations required to support classified work at scale.

We’re looking for someone who brings deep special programs expertise, sound operational judgment, and the credibility to work directly with government customers and senior internal stakeholders. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone comfortable navigating ambiguity, helping build the function, mentoring future team members, and finding compliant paths forward when mission needs and security requirements intersect.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, or Washington, DC. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. Additional onsite presence and occasional travel may be required based on classified program, facility, and government customer needs.

This position requires active Top Secret eligibility, current SCI access, and a current counterintelligence (CI) polygraph at the time of application. Candidates must also be able to obtain and maintain additional customer-required accesses, including a full-scope polygraph if required.

In This Role, You Will

Lead SCI and SAP security operations across the program lifecycle, including access administration, indoctrinations and debriefings, security plans, classification requirements, incident reporting, inspections, and program closeout.
Serve as the designated CSSO, CPSO, or equivalent program security official for assigned government customers and classified programs.
Build and maintain trusted relationships with Intelligence Community and Department of Defense customers, government security officers, program security officers, and other external security stakeholders.
Oversee the establishment, accreditation, operation, modification, and inspection readiness of Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities and Special Access Program Facilities.
Translate government regulations, contract requirements, DD Forms 254, security classification guides, and customer direction into practical policies, procedures, and operating decisions.
Coordinate closely with personnel security, information systems security, classified IT, Facilities, Legal, and program teams to establish clear ownership and integrated safeguards.
Lead self-inspections, security inquiries, corrective actions, customer assessments, and escalation of risks that could affect access, accreditation, or program execution.
Advise Industrial Security leadership, independently represent the security function, and provide operational continuity across critical programs and customer relationships.
Mentor and develop special programs security personnel while establishing the staffing, metrics, governance, and operating rhythms needed to support continued growth.
Enable classified work through risk-informed decisions while maintaining the judgment and authority to stop or escalate activity that would violate security requirements.

You Might Thrive In This Role If You

Have substantial experience leading contractor security for SCI and SAP programs, including direct experience as a CSSO, CPSO, CSPSO, SSO, or comparable customer-designated security official.
Understand how Intelligence Community customers operate, including sponsor relationships, access processes, reciprocity, customer-specific requirements, and appropriate escalation channels.
Have strong working knowledge of the NISPOM, ICDs 703, 704, and 705, Intelligence Community technical specifications for SCIFs, DoDM 5205.07, applicable Security Executive Agent Directives, and related customer guidance.
Have established, accredited, operated, or modified SCIFs or SAPFs and can coordinate facility, physical security, information security, and technical accreditation requirements.
Have successfully managed government customer relationships and can communicate clearly with security officials, technical teams, program leaders, and senior executives.
Have led security inspections, customer reviews, incident response, corrective actions, and closure of complex compliance findings.
Exercise strong judgment under pressure and can distinguish between requirements that can be addressed creatively and boundaries that cannot be crossed.
Enjoy building teams, improving operating models, clarifying ownership, and creating durable processes in fast-moving environments, and are eager to use approved AI tools, agents, and automations to reduce administrative burden, improve visibility, and scale sound judgment without replacing sponsor approvals, security authority, or required human review.
Hold active Top Secret eligibility and current SCI access with a current counterintelligence polygraph, and can obtain and maintain a full-scope polygraph or other customer-required access.
Bring additional experience across multiple Intelligence Community or SAP customers, industrial security program buildouts, COMSEC, insider threat, or related security leadership disciplines.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products.
